description: Aerospace engineering students passionate about bioastronautics and space systems. We're building health monitoring software to track vital signs and assess risks in microgravity for long-duration missions. Let’s team up!
summary: In deep space, microgravity and cosmic radiation take a heavy toll on the human body, causing muscle atrophy, heart problems, and a weakened immune system. Worse yet, a 20 minute communication delay with Earth means astronauts cannot wait for ground control during a medical crisis. To solve this, we built SpaceMed, an onboard health monitoring software created with HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and C++ (using VS Code and GitHub) that connects directly to spacesuits or takes manual inputs. Our system tackles daily health risks by tracking vital signs (NLSP), checking muscle density (SLAMMD/NLSP), and calculating radiation exposure through active silicon dosimeters and open NASA data. If an emergency happens, our interface includes an emergency protocol that can be used immediately without needing to scan or pass the astronaut's security check. This project matters because it gives astronauts instant, independent medical support when Earth is out of reach. Looking ahead, we really hope to integrate the ELISA MABL system in the future so crews can analyze biological samples in microgravity, measuring antibodies, antigens, and proteins to catch health issues early on long-duration missions.
details: It monitors the crew’s health status and provides instant medical recommendations, in addition to identifying possible diseases or conditions based on the symptoms presented. It operates in conjunction with the biometric data from the spacesuits and, in emergencies, through manual entry of biometric data. Since this data is constantly updated, it helps cross-reference information and generate a health history to detect anomalies. There is also an emergency section that provides immediate medical recommendations and cross-references data with potential conditions based on symptoms. One of the major benefits is that it helps prevent potential health issues by anticipating them based on symptom patterns, in addition to providing a series of steps to take in the event of an emergency. It is hoped that this software will be able to accurately predict potential health conditions by correlating data over time; furthermore, it is anticipated that in the future, more specific biomarkers with greater precision regarding these conditions will be utilized. The programming languages used were JavaScript, HTML, and CSS; Visual Studio was used to view and modify the code, and GitHub was used to publish the website.
